purpose: Legacy Forge operation surface -> canonical Legion operation identity. S01 action 3 requires legacy assess/checkpoint/verify/close observable behavior be preserved where it does not conflict with stronger Arcane invariants; action 4 requires every conflict be an explicit compatibility error, never a silent weakening; action 7 requires compatibility aliases contain no independent policy decisions.
aliasRule: A compatibility alias performs exactly one job: translate shapes and forward. It evaluates no policy, chooses no authority, and grants no trust. Every allow/deny answer comes from the single Arcane policy bundle (policy/arcane-policy-v1.json) so no adapter can hold divergent logic (S02 acceptance: 'adapters do not contain divergent allow/deny logic').

operationEnvelope.note: operation-envelope-v1 is a $defs-only schema: validate against the OperationRequest / OperationResult definitions, not against the file's (empty) top level.

preservedBehavior: Returns a run handle and a budget projection to the caller.
Trigger scoring remains available as compatibility-only output; it drives nothing canonical.

conflicts.legacy: assess accepts caller-supplied `authority` and stores it on the run row.
conflicts.arcaneInvariant: Authority identity is asserted by the kernel per turn, never claimed by the model in text (ARCHITECTURE §24a).
conflicts.resolution: Compatibility error ARC_AUTHORITY_MODEL_CLAIMED when the alias payload carries an `authority` field. The alias does not silently drop it and does not silently honor it.

operations.canonicalResult: OperationResult carrying the recorded evidence ids and any invalidation event id
preservedBehavior: invalidated_keys[] still stales matching evidence — mapped onto DependencyLedger.observeChange with dimension 'opaque-legacy-key' (S05).
A `failure` object still consumes retry budget and can block when exhausted.

conflicts.legacy: checkpoint under authority='host' with a non-empty `receipt` string mints tool-trust evidence and can set a check to passed, with zero structural validation of that receipt (lib/core.js:493-494, 536-539).
conflicts.arcaneInvariant: Only host-observed, structurally valid, S03-verified events become receipts (S00 finding 5; S04).
conflicts.resolution: Compatibility error ARC_HOST_EVENT_UNTRUSTED. The evidence is still recorded — as an unauthenticated legacy envelope with no canonical trust — so the caller does not lose data, but it never becomes qualifying evidence.

conflicts.legacy: Caller may supply failure.error_fingerprint and thereby choose its own retry-budget key (lib/budget.js:46-51).
conflicts.arcaneInvariant: Retry fingerprints are derived from host-observed effect data (S04 action 9).
conflicts.resolution: The supplied fingerprint is retained as compatibility metadata; the canonical fingerprint is recomputed. Divergence is reported, not hidden.

operations.criticality: README.md:114 — 'the exit code of verify --gate signoff is the enforcement surface' for CI.
operations.canonicalResult: OperationResult with claimBoundary + deficits as blocker-v1 entries
preservedBehavior: Gate semantics survive as policy claim levels: `signoff` -> policy.claimLevels.signoff, `high_risk` -> policy.claimLevels.highRisk.
Exit-code contract preserved for CI: non-zero on a blocked gate.
refreshAttestations' re-hash-on-verify behavior is preserved and GENERALIZED by the S05 ledger (which re-checks every bound dimension, not only the locator file).

conflicts.legacy: A gate can pass on evidence whose trust came from an unvalidated host receipt.
conflicts.arcaneInvariant: Claim prerequisites are validated against authenticated evidence only (ARCHITECTURE §26: Arcane validates prerequisites and controls release).
conflicts.resolution: Gate outcome is recomputed from canonical evidence. A legacy-passing gate may evaluate to blocked under Arcane; that is a strengthening and is reported explicitly, never suppressed.

preservedBehavior: Idempotent close: re-closing an already-closed run returns the original terminal result (fixture 12-close-idempotent-response.json) rather than erroring.
close still refuses when the signoff gate is unsatisfied (fixture 07-close-blocked-response.json).

conflicts.legacy: close_ledger_hash is computed by the same process that wrote the ledger.
conflicts.arcaneInvariant: Tamper evidence must be independently verifiable (detailed plan §5.2).
conflicts.resolution: close still returns close_ledger_hash for compatibility, but canonical integrity is the Arcane receipt-store prev-digest chain, verified by ReceiptStore.verifyChain(). The legacy hash is not treated as evidence of anything.

operations.canonicalResult: run identity or an explicit unbound result
preservedBehavior: The 'sole open run' heuristic stays RETIRED (lib/core.js:209-212). An unbound session resolves to unbound. This legacy behavior is stronger than guessing and is preserved verbatim.
Read-only; never initializes a store (S00 confirmed by a passing Forge test).

conflicts.legacy: doctor reports environment facts but never states an enforcement level.
conflicts.arcaneInvariant: A host without working interception cannot be labeled `strong`; Arcane reports its own degradation honestly, typed, per capability (ARCHITECTURE §24a).
conflicts.resolution: Extended, not weakened: the canonical operation additionally returns a per-capability enforcement level. No legacy output field is removed.

operations.reason: Destructive, unconfirmed, and authenticated by nothing beyond the same model-only CLI ceiling as every other command; deletes every row matching a run id across all tables. It contradicts the append-only history requirement (detailed plan §5.3: 'never truncate history merely to get a green result'). No canonical successor. Calling the alias returns a typed compatibility error.

conflicts.arcaneInvariant: Append-only logical event history; corruption is quarantined, not truncated.
conflicts.resolution: Explicit rejection. Retention/expiry is a policy concern (policy.retention), executed as expiry of unlinked candidates, never as an unauthenticated caller-triggered delete.

operations.reason: ARCHITECTURE §24a: Arcane 'does not absorb Forge's product expansion (no second daemon, no docs-provider hub, no separate CLI, no competing lifecycle store).' The docs resolver is product expansion, not enforcement lineage. Listed here so the omission is explicit rather than an oversight.

operations.legacySurface: MCP legacy tools, active only under FORGE_LEGACY_TOOLS=1 (server.js:11,431)
operations.reason: Already deprecated/compat-only in Forge and disabled by default. S00 flagged the tension between docs/store-migration.md:3 ('Current Forge accepts no legacy ... MCP tool ... alias') and the flag still existing with test coverage. No canonical successor; no alias is provided.

operations.legacyOperation: hook dispatch (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop)

mapping.SessionStart: arcane.gate.prePrompt (bind authority identity for the turn)

preservedBehavior: PostToolUse success is still NOT recorded as a passing check (hooks/generic/hook.js:99-101). This legacy restraint is correct and is preserved: S04 classifies a successful tool call as an observation, never as proof.

conflicts.legacy: A handler exceeding its 1500ms budget is marked bypassed_delayed_verifier and the dispatcher CONTINUES past it (lib/dispatcher.js:29-37) — enforcement can be skipped purely on a timeout, fail-open.
conflicts.arcaneInvariant: If the pre-effect gate is unavailable, mutation-bearing operations fail closed; read-only operations may continue with a recorded enforcement-health downgrade (ARCHITECTURE §24a).
conflicts.resolution: NOT preserved. This is the single most important behavioral divergence in this map. Arcane's pre-effect gate returns ARC_GATE_UNAVAILABLE with failClosed:true for mutation-bearing effect classes on timeout/unavailability, and a recorded downgrade for read-only ones. Legacy callers relying on fail-open will observe denials they did not previously get; that is the intended strengthening.

aliasPolicyAudit.requirement: S01 action 7 / S02 acceptance — compatibility aliases contain no independent policy decisions.
aliasPolicyAudit.method: lib/legacy-bridge.mjs contains no allow/deny branch. Every decision-shaped answer it returns originates from lib/policy.mjs or lib/pre-effect-gate.mjs. tests/s01-bridge.test.mjs asserts the bridge module's source contains no policy-decision literals.
